evals.prompt: Review this Rust segment intersection: it branches on a raw f64 cross product, computes the point, clamps t into [0,1], and later decides endpoint identity with distance < 1e-6. Recommend the smallest robust redesign.
evals.expected_output: A predicate-first, certified-construction redesign with an explicit exact-zero/endpoint policy and no epsilon-based topology override.
expectations: Separates topological classification from coordinate construction.
Uses filtered-exact predicate signs for represented inputs and names exact zero as a policy case.
Rejects silent parameter clamping and validates construction parameters/residuals against a numerical bound.
Does not present one generic epsilon or the golden output as the correctness authority.

evals.prompt: Design property tests for a slicer under translation, rotation, reflection, uniform scale, and non-uniform affine transforms. The slicer uses fixed world-Z layers and anisotropic process settings.
evals.expected_output: Preconditioned metamorphic properties that transform the slicing frame and dimensional/process parameters correctly rather than asserting false mesh-only symmetry.
expectations: Explains why arbitrary Z translation or mesh-only rotation is not invariant with fixed world-Z layers.
Scales dimensional tolerances/process parameters under uniform scaling but not dimensionless relative tolerances.
Handles reflection orientation reversal and inverse-transpose normal transformation.
Uses numerical residual bounds for inverse round trips instead of byte equality.

evals.prompt: Our Linux CI hashes g-code twice and our cross-platform numeric goldens use tolerances. Can we claim deterministic and treat the blessed files as correct? Define a defensible contract and review gate.
evals.expected_output: Named determinism tiers and an authority hierarchy in which specs/invariants/oracles outrank snapshots.
expectations: Distinguishes canonical/topological, pinned-byte, and cross-platform-byte determinism.
States that a two-run hash proves neither cross-platform bytes nor geometric correctness.
Requires exact topology/order comparison and field tolerances unless a byte tier applies.
Requires blessing justification from a higher authority and forbids silent regeneration.
